models.name: ForbiddenErrorInsightSchemaValueRefusalBasis
models.description:
Always present. **Treat this as an open set**: the values below are the ones Truto
emits today, and the read path deliberately accepts an unrecognised one so a newly
shipped state cannot break a client — or an older Truto build — that has not heard
of it. Generate a permissive type from it and keep a default branch.

`scopes_missing` — the scopes in `missing_scopes` are absent from the grant, and a
re-consent flow is the remedy. `scopes_satisfied` — every declared scope is
granted, so the refusal has another cause. `non_scope_requirement` — the
requirement is a role or API-key permission, named in `required_permissions`, so
reconnecting will not change it. `no_scope_concept` — this connection's auth method
has no OAuth scopes at all, so there is nothing to grant and reconnecting cannot
help. `not_determined` — no comparison ran and Truto cannot name a basis; read
`description` for which of the reasons applied, and `raw_response` for the
provider's own account.

Each value leads somewhere different, in what a reader is told AND in what remedy
is worth offering. Where two states differed only in why Truto had no answer they
are one state here, and the difference survives in `description`.

A closed `enum` here, unlike on `last_forbidden_error.refusal_basis`, because a
running build always emits its own documented set — this value is computed per
request, never read back from storage. A build that ships a sixth state ships this
list with it.

models.name: RemoteErrorResponseSchema
models.description:
The body Truto returns when a **third-party API** refused the call, rather than Truto
itself. Identified by `truto_is_remote_error`.

This is the envelope `truto_error_insight` arrives in. It is a **`components/schemas`
entry that no operation references**, deliberately, and the reason is worth stating so it
is not "fixed" by hanging it off an unrelated route: the operations that return it are the
Unified API and Proxy API data routes, and neither is enumerated here. The Unified API's
paths and payloads are generated per unified model and per integration, so there is no
fixed operation to attach. The Proxy API's paths are fixed (`/proxy/{resource}`) but are
not documented in this specification at all — a pre-existing gap, and documenting them is
its own piece of work.

A `components/responses` wrapper used to sit beside this. It was removed: nothing could
reference it either, so it added a second unreachable node rather than a route into this
one. Mainstream generators emit every `components/schemas` entry as a named type whether or
not a path reaches it, so this shape is importable today; a generator that prunes
unreferenced schemas will not see it, and until the routes above are documented that is the
honest state of affairs rather than something a `$ref` can paper over.

The shape itself is fixed, and is what a client should type those calls against. See the
Errors guide for the full list of insight keys.

fields.name: message
fields.description:
The human text pulled out of the provider's own error body.

**Unbounded, and not always a sentence.** The extractor's last candidate is the payload
itself when the payload is a string, so for a plain-text or HTML error body this field
is the entire body — 34 KB is a real observed value. Size it accordingly, or truncate
before display. `raw_response_excerpt` on `last_forbidden_error` is the only capped
copy of a provider body Truto stores.

fields.name: truto_is_remote_error
fields.description:
`true` when the third-party API produced this error. When absent or `false`, Truto
rejected the request before it left the edge.

fields.name: raw_response
fields.description:
The integration's error body, verbatim and uninterpreted. An object for a JSON body, a
string for a plain-text or HTML one. Present on every remote error.

fields.name: format
fields.description: Optional format hint (e.g. `date-time`, `uuid`). On a `body_schema` property, `type: string` + `format: binary` declares FILE BYTES. The rule, exactly: the property is TOP-LEVEL (or the `items` of a top-level array of files, `multipart` only; Elaichi does not send multipart arrays as files yet, which needs `noSquareBrackets: true` on the method and cardamom#30, so a single file field works today and the lint warns on an array) and is `type: string` (an untyped `{format: binary}` is not a file), and the method's effective body is `multipart` (a file part named after the property) or `raw` (the ONE property of the body, under a content type that is not a data format; an array of files is not read under `raw`). The effective body is the engine's: an unset `body_format` means `json` for a `list` method and a DELETE `delete`, and NO body for every other method, and `multipart` on list/get/delete or `raw` on get/delete is not built at all. `format: binary` on a `json`/`form`/`xml` body (or a method that sends no body) is not read as a file; a file carried as base64 text in a `json`/`form` body uses `contentEncoding` instead.

fields.name: contentEncoding
fields.description: JSON Schema `contentEncoding`. On a TOP-LEVEL `type: string` property (or the `items` of a top-level array) of a `json` or `form` `body_schema`, `base64` / `base64url` (case-insensitive) declares that the string carries a file's content encoded as text (for example Microsoft Graph `contentBytes`). Elaichi reads it in `json` and `form` bodies and also as a scalar part in `multipart`; it is not read in `raw` (the body is the bytes, declared with `format: binary`) or `xml`, and a multipart ARRAY of encoded parts is deferred like an array of files. `format: byte` alone is not a file. Never combine it with `format: binary`.

models.description:

fields.description: Static or templated query-string params merged with caller-supplied `query`. Values may be strings, numbers, booleans, arrays, or placeholders. Array serialization is controlled by `query_array_format`.

fields.name: query_array_format
fields.description: How array values are serialized in the query string. `comma` → `?a=1,2`; `brackets` → `?a[]=1&a[]=2`; `indices` → `?a[0]=1&a[1]=2`; `repeat` → `?a=1&a=2`.

The runtime (see `src/mcp/mcpRouter.ts`) reads `body_schema.properties`, so callers should emit the wrapped `JsonSchemaObject` shape `{ type "object", properties { ... } }` rather than a flat `{ name { type "string" } }` map.

fields.description:

  * `json` — JSON-encoded (default).
  * `form` — `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`.
  * `multipart` — `multipart/form-data`. See `IntegrationResourceMethodBodyFormatConfigMultipart` for tuning options. The file field is declared in `body_schema` as `type: string, format: binary`.
  * `raw` — sent verbatim, with `Content-Type` set from `body_format_config.content_type`. fields.description: Extra options for the chosen `body_format`. Discriminated by the sibling `body_format` field — see `IntegrationResourceMethodBodyFormatConfigRaw` (for `raw`) and `IntegrationResourceMethodBodyFormatConfigMultipart` (for `multipart`). fields.name: response_schema
fields.description: JSON-schema-style declaration of the response payload used by Truto's MCP/tooling.

fields.name: response_path
fields.description: Dotted-path accessor (e.g. `data.results`, `payload.users.*`, `result.0.items`) into the parsed response that contains the canonical resource (or array of resources). Defaults to the root. This is a path lookup, **not** a JSONata expression.

fields.name: pagination
fields.description: Override the integration-level pagination for this single method. Set to `null` to disable pagination on a method that would otherwise inherit it.

fields.name: add_query_to_body
fields.description: For `post`/`put`/`patch` methods, copy the caller-supplied query params into the body before sending.

fields.name: ignore_body_in_pagination
fields.description: Don't re-send the body when fetching subsequent pagination pages.

fields.name: ignore_body
fields.description: Drop the body entirely (useful for vendors that 400 on empty bodies).

fields.name: set_body_to_null
fields.description: Send a literal JSON `null` instead of an empty body.

fields.name: no_auth
fields.description: Skip applying the integration's authorization to this method (e.g. a public health check).

fields.name: ignore_credentials_on_redirect
fields.description: Strip the Authorization header when the upstream issues a redirect to a different host.

fields.name: api_response_format
fields.description: Override the response parser (e.g. `xml`, `text`).

fields.name: throw_error_on_parse_error
fields.description: When true, fail loudly if the response can't be parsed; otherwise return a structured error.

fields.name: error_expression
fields.description:
JSONata expression evaluated on every response (success or failure). Use to detect errors in successful (2xx) responses, normalize error messages, or transform "errors" with `< 400` status into successful responses with the `result` you return.

Input: `IntegrationErrorExpressionContext`. Output: `IntegrationErrorExpressionResult` — return `null`/`undefined` to indicate "no error", or a `{ status, message?, headers?, metadata?, result? }` object.

fields.name: description
fields.description: Human-readable description of the method, used in MCP tool listings.

fields.name: api_documentation_url
fields.description: URL to the upstream vendor's documentation for this method.

fields.name: scopes
fields.description:
Permissions required to call this method, **all** of which are needed. Usually OAuth
scopes, but an integration that issues no OAuth grant, or whose permissions are role
names, writes those here instead — which vocabulary is in use is derived from the
integration, or declared here with `permission_vocabulary`.

fields.name: scopes_any_of
fields.description:
Permissions of which holding **any one** is enough, kept apart from `scopes` (which is
all-of). Providers say so explicitly — Microsoft Graph answers a 403 with "API requires
one of 'Chat.ReadBasic.All, Chat.Read.All, Chat.ReadWrite.All'" — and treating that as
all-of reports scopes as missing that the operation never needed.

fields.name: permission_vocabulary
fields.description:
Which vocabulary `scopes` and `scopes_any_of` above are written in, declared rather
than inferred. Normally omitted: Truto derives this from configuration that already
exists, so every integration is classified without anyone labelling it. Set it only to
correct a derivation that reads an integration wrongly.

It exists because the derivation is deliberately whole-integration — an author writes
one list in one vocabulary throughout, and only some entries carry the proof — which
makes it correct for every integration in production and unable to express an
exception. `jamf` is the exception: nine methods declare console role labels
(`Read - Users`) and `users.create` declares a real OAuth scope (`users:create`), and
no integration-wide answer is right for both. Declaring it on the one method leaves the
other eighty untouched.

An unrecognised value falls back to the derivation rather than being reported to a
customer.

fields.name: mcp_annotations
fields.description:
Hints mirroring MCP `ToolAnnotations` for this method's tool, read by consumers that
classify tools (e.g. Elaichi) to decide read, write or destructive. Keys keep the MCP
spec's camelCase spelling on purpose. Absent means "no hint": consumers fall back to
their existing rules, and a missing flag is not read as `false`. `readOnlyHint` and
`destructiveHint` cannot both be `true`.

fields.name: before
fields.description:
Steps to run before this method's own request: an array of steps run in order, or a
string naming a sibling method whose steps are reused. Same step shape as a unified
model mapping's `before`. Accepted and stored so engines that run proxy configs can
execute it; **Truto's own proxy does not run it yet**, so on Truto this is inert.
Each step's `run_if` must parse as JSONata, or the write is a 400.

fields.name: body
fields.description: Static or templated request body for `post`/`put`/`patch` methods. Any JSON value (usually an object, sometimes an array) and may include placeholders. Use `$truto_merge` with `:json` to deep-merge an entire object; see placeholder syntax.

models.name: IntegrationWebhookSignatureVerification
models.description:
Strategy used to verify an inbound webhook's signature. The `format` discriminator selects which `config` shape applies.

All string values inside `config` support Truto placeholders resolved against the inbound webhook `IntegrationWebhookPayloadContext` (`{{body.foo}}`, `{{headers.x-signature}}`, `{{raw_body}}`, `{{context.api_key}}`, etc.).

models.name: IntegrationWebhookConfig
models.description: How Truto receives and verifies inbound webhooks for this integration. **Not** to be confused with `WebhookSchema` elsewhere in this spec, which describes Truto's _outbound_ webhook delivered to your application.

fields.name: signature_verification
fields.description: Strategy used to verify the webhook signature before accepting it. Runs **after** `payload_transform` and **after** `handle_verification` returns `{ type: 'payload' }`.

fields.name: handle_verification
fields.description:
JSONata expression evaluated on **every** inbound webhook before signature verification. Use to:
  * Respond to handshake pings (return `{ type: 'verify', verification_response: { status_code, body, headers } }`).
  * Surface meta-events that should not fan out (return `{ type: 'meta' }`).
  * Update the integrated account context (return `{ type: 'verify' \| 'payload' \| 'meta', update_context: { ... } }`).
  * Pass through to fan-out (return `{ type: 'payload' }` or omit entirely — defaults to `payload`).

Input: `IntegrationWebhookPayloadContext`. Output: `IntegrationWebhookHandleVerificationResult`.

fields.name: payload_transform
fields.description:
JSONata expression that transforms the raw inbound payload **before** `handle_verification` and `signature_verification` see it. Use to normalize vendor-specific envelopes (e.g. unwrap a Salesforce `payloads[]` array, decode a base64 body).

Input: `IntegrationWebhookPayloadContext`. Output: `IntegrationWebhookPayloadContext` (the same shape — what you return becomes the new payload).

fields.description:
Integration-wide JSONata expression evaluated on every response. Use to detect errors in successful (2xx) responses, normalize error messages, or transform "errors" with `< 400` status into successful responses. Overridden by per-method `IntegrationResourceMethod.error_expression` when set.

Input: `IntegrationErrorExpressionContext`. Output: `IntegrationErrorExpressionResult` — return `null`/`undefined` to indicate "no error", or a `{ status, message?, headers?, metadata?, result? }` object.

fields.name: browser_file_picker_requires_access_token
fields.description:
This provider's **browser** file picker cannot run without the connected account's upstream `access_token`, so `GET /integrated-account/me` releases `context.oauth.token.access_token` — and nothing else — to a connect-flow integrated account token. Google Drive and Box need it; their picker SDKs take the token client-side. SharePoint, OneDrive and Dropbox authenticate by other means and must leave this unset.

A `refresh_token` is never released, whatever this is set to. Honoured only on the integration's own `config`: it is not part of `EnvironmentIntegrationConfig`, and it is stripped from an integrated account's `integration_override`, so it cannot be switched on for a single environment or account.

fields.name: oauth_app_headers
fields.description:
Headers built from the connected account's OAuth app and sent on every request, for providers that want the app's own key next to the user's token. Etsy, for example, needs `{ "x-api-key": "{{client.id}}:{{client.secret}}" }`.

A value may use `{{client.id}}` and `{{client.secret}}` — the OAuth client the account's token was issued to, read and filled in as the token refresh does — and no other placeholder. Saving an integration fails with a 400 if a value uses any other placeholder, or if a header name is one that debug output echoes back (`x-truto-*`, `content-type`, `accept`, `user-agent` and similar).

A header that can't be filled completely is left out: a client field it uses is unset, or is still a placeholder the account's context can't fill. Added after `authorization`, replacing a header of the same name in any letter case. Only accounts connected with `oauth2` get these headers, and a method with `no_auth` doesn't.

Honoured only on the integration's own `config`: it is not part of `EnvironmentIntegrationConfig`, and it is stripped from an integrated account's `integration_override`.

A header that uses `{{client.secret}}` is sent only to the sites of the requests configured by whoever set that secret: the integration, or an environment's override over it. An environment or account override that keeps that app but sends requests elsewhere (its own `base_url`, a method's URL, an `authorization` expression, a mapping's path) sends them without these headers. Through a Static Gate, the target URL counts. An account's own secret (in its `integration_override`, or filled in from its context) goes wherever its requests go.

fields.name: missing_scopes
fields.description:
The scopes required by this resource and method that the provider did not confirm as
granted.

Present only when both halves of that comparison are known: the provider echoed the
scopes it granted, **and** this resource and method declares required scopes. It is
**absent** — not empty — otherwise, which includes `api_key` and OAuth1 connections
(no scope grant exists), OAuth2 and `jwt_bearer` connections where the provider
omits `scope` from its token response, resources and methods that declare no
required scopes, and requirements that are not OAuth scopes at all
(`refusal_basis: non_scope_requirement` — see `permission_vocabulary`), where no
diff is run and `required_permissions` carries the answer instead.

An empty array therefore means "no *all-of* scope is missing", while an absent
field means "cannot be determined" — two different statements. Read `refusal_basis`
for the one question this field cannot answer on its own, "was anything missing at
all": an empty array sits beside a populated `missing_any_of_scopes` whenever the
whole shortfall is an unmet any-of requirement, so on
`refusal_basis: scopes_missing` an empty array does **not** mean every permission
was granted. It means that on `refusal_basis: scopes_satisfied`, and only there. Do
not default an absent `missing_scopes` to `[]` either: that reads back as "nothing
is missing" about a request that was refused.

Truto's comparison is an inference over integration configuration. The provider's
own account of the refusal is the authoritative one, and Truto relays it without
interpreting it: `raw_response` (the error body verbatim) and `message` (its human
text) on the 403 itself, and a capped copy of the body on this record as
`raw_response_excerpt`. `message` is not persisted, so re-run the call to see it.

Truto deliberately does not lift a "code" or a "documentation link" out of that
body. Which key in an arbitrary provider's error shape is the important one has no
correct general answer, and a confidently wrong one placed above a correct body is
the same failure as reporting a scope missing that was never checked.

fields.name: refusal_basis
fields.description:
Which of the states below produced this record, so a reader never has to infer it
from the presence or emptiness of `missing_scopes`. Absent on rows recorded before
Truto stored it — and on such a row an empty `missing_scopes` cannot be read as
"compared, nothing missing", because it was also written when nothing had been
compared at all.

**An open set, and `x-extensible-enum` rather than `enum` says so to a code
generator as well as to a reader.** Prose asking for a default branch is not
something a generator reads, and a closed union here can be violated by design:
the read path deliberately accepts an unrecognised value so a row written by a
newer build stays readable after a rollback, and the older build then serves that
value straight back on this field. The values below are what Truto writes today.
Keep a default branch.

The live `truto_error_insight.forbidden_error.value.refusal_basis` keeps a closed
`enum`, and the asymmetry is the point: a running build always emits its own
documented set, while a stored row can carry a value the build reading it never
wrote.

fields.name: description
fields.description: The sentence the live 403 carried, recorded so this row reads the same as the call did.

fields.name: missing_any_of_scopes
fields.description:

apart from `missing_scopes` so alternatives are never reported as though all were
required.

fields.name: required_permissions
fields.description:
What this operation requires, whether or not a comparison was possible. Always
paired with `permission_vocabulary`, since the same string means "reconnect and
grant this", "add this to your API key" or "ask an admin for this role" depending
on which vocabulary it is written in.

fields.name: required_any_of_permissions
fields.description: Permissions of which the operation needs *any one*, kept apart from `required_permissions` for the same reason.

fields.name: permission_vocabulary
fields.description:
Which vocabulary `required_permissions` is written in, and therefore what the
remedy is. Only `oauth_scope` is fixed by reconnecting: `api_key_permission` is
granted to the API key in the provider, and `role_label` in the provider's own
admin console.

`x-extensible-enum` for the same reason as `refusal_basis` above: this is a stored
value, and a rollback can serve one written by a build that knew a fourth
vocabulary. Keep a default branch.

fields.name: raw_response_excerpt
fields.description:
A capped copy of the integration's own error body, so this record shows what the
provider said and not only what Truto inferred about it. Truncated with a trailing
`… truncated` marker past 2,048 **bytes** of UTF-8, because this record is
deserialized on every proxy and unified call that resolves the account and that cost
is what the bound exists to control. Bytes, not characters: 2,048 characters of CJK
is about 6 KB stored, so a character bound would charge one language three times
what it charges another. Expect fewer characters than 2,048 for any non-ASCII body.
The 2,048 covers the marker as well, so the stored value never exceeds it.

**A truncated excerpt is not parseable.** It is a byte prefix of a serialized body
with a marker on the end, so `JSON.parse` on this field throws whenever truncation
happened — which the trailing `… truncated` is how you detect. Render it as text.
An untruncated excerpt of a JSON body does parse, but nothing guarantees this field
is JSON at all: a plain-text or HTML error body is stored exactly as it arrived.

Absent when the refusal carried no body. Not forwarded to the connections widget:
it is a raw provider string, which is what `connections.show_error_details` exists
to keep away from an end user.

Note that "every remote 403 carries an insight" and "every remote 403 leaves a
record here" are different statements. A Proxy API **custom method** and a **Custom
API** both carry the live insight, but a Custom API names no resource or method, and
writing `{resource: "", method: ""}` would replace a record naming a real call with
one naming none — so no record is written for those. Read the insight on the
response for them.

models.name: IntegrationGeneratedField
models.description:
A single value Truto generates once per connection, declared in a credential's `config.generated_fields` array. Used where the provider requires the value to be produced by Truto rather than by the customer. It is generated for the connection and kept for its life — a reconnect never regenerates it, and a caller-supplied value for the same name is ignored.

- `uuid` — a public value such as an AWS IAM role's External ID, which pins the customer's role trust policy to Truto. Written to the top level of the integrated-account context under `name` and read from placeholders as `{{<name>}}`, exactly like a `config.fields` entry. It is not a credential and is not redacted.
- `rsa_key_pair` — Truto makes an RSA key pair for the connection. Only the **public** half is stored under `name` — `{ public_key, public_key_pem, fingerprint, key_id, key_id_short, created_at }` — and shown to the customer to install in the provider. The **private** half is a credential: it is encrypted, never returned by any API, and never visible to placeholders, mappings or expressions; only a `jwt_bearer` credential that names it in `signing.generated` can sign with it. It cannot be declared on a credential that connects through a browser redirect, or in an integrated account's own `integration_override`.

`name` must be letters, digits and underscores, must not start with `truto_`, and must not be a key Truto stores a secret under (`api_key`, `token`, `oauth`, `secret`, `generated_secrets`, …).

An environment override that sets `generated_fields` replaces the integration's list rather than adding to it, like every other array in an override, so it has to repeat any key pair the integration declares. Truto refuses an override that would leave `signing.generated` naming a key pair the credential no longer declares.
